title: Order fulfilment
goal: Show a complete e-commerce order path from intake through dispatch with realistic exceptions.

rubric.must: A payment-authorisation decision visibly sends a No branch to a cancelled-order terminator.
An inventory-availability decision visibly separates the pick-and-pack path from a backorder-or-refund path.
The successful path visibly runs from reserved inventory through pick list, picking, packing, carrier collection, and dispatch.
A customer-accepted backorder visibly loops back toward inventory reservation.
A failed carrier collection visibly leads to a hold step that loops back to collection confirmation.
Decision branches are visibly labelled so the success and failure outcomes can be distinguished.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the flowchart exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The target shows a complete, traceable order flow from intake through dispatch, with visible payment, inventory, backorder, and carrier exceptions. Labels are readable and branches are marked; no material overlap or cropping is apparent.

items.evidence: “Payment authorised?” has a labelled No branch to “Notify payment failure,” then to the “Order cancelled” terminator.
“All items available?” separates a labelled Yes branch into “Release pick list” and a No branch into “Offer backorder or refund.”
The Yes path from inventory reservation proceeds through release pick list, pick items, pack and label, carrier collection confirmation, and dispatch shipment.
Accepting the backorder leads to “Create replenishment order,” with a dashed rework loop returning toward “Reserve inventory.”
The No branch from “Carrier collection confirmed?” leads to “Hold for next collection,” whose dashed loop returns to the collection decision.
Decision branches are visibly marked Yes and No, and the labels and flowchart text are readable.
